strengths: The paper addresses a timely and important question in mechanistic interpretability—how LLMs represent and process numeric and ordinal information—and convincingly demonstrates that sinusoidal structures are shared across diverse model families (Llama 3, OLMo 2, Phi 4) and sizes (1B to 15B).

The proposed `param-sin` probe offers a principled inductive bias by explicitly parameterizing the frequency, phase, and amplitude of sine features, yielding higher decoding accuracy, superior parameter efficiency, and better out-of-distribution generalization compared to prior probes.

A significant methodological improvement over previous literature is the evaluation on ~700k natural-language contexts across multiple domains (culinary, arithmetic, medical, temporal), showing that probes trained on natural text generalize much better across distribution shifts than probes trained strictly on synthetic arithmetic prompts.

The mechanistic experiments go beyond passive probing: the authors show that sinusoidal structure relates directly to computational correctness, demonstrate multi-token superposition, and validate the functional relevance of these representations via activation steering and layer-intervention experiments.
weaknesses: Several figures (especially Figures 1, 2, 5a, and 17) have very small text, axes, and colorbars that are difficult to read in the standard PDF layout.
A few placeholder links/URLs are left blank in the text (e.g., footnote 1 on page 2 and the repository link in Appendix B).

The layer-dropping experiment described in Section A.8 is preliminary and somewhat ad-hoc, with the authors themselves noting that its practical applicability is constrained by low absolute numbers of correct predictions at earlier layers.

The universality claims are evaluated solely on standard English-centric autoregressive decoder Transformers trained on similar web distributions; testing non-standard tokenization schemes or non-autoregressive architectures would further substantiate the claim of architectural universality.

strengths: The paper significantly expands prior interpretability literature on numerical representations (which was predominantly restricted to synthetic addition and isolated token embeddings) by evaluating across natural language contexts, multiple arithmetic operations (including multiplication and division), and multi-token numbers.

The proposed `param-sin` probe architecture is theoretically principled and well-motivated, parameterizing frequencies, phase-shifts, and amplitudes directly; it consistently matches or outperforms existing linear and fixed-basis sinusoidal probes across models and layers.

The analysis of cross-model and cross-layer universality is thorough, spanning multiple model families (Llama, OLMo, Phi) and sizes, supported by quantitative representational similarity analysis (RSA) and Fourier frequency overlap metrics.

The work does not stop at correlational probing; it validates functional relevance via mechanistic intervention (activation steering and layer ablation), demonstrating that steering representations toward sinusoidal target patterns can correct model calculation errors.
weaknesses: The fundamental observation that language models encode numbers and arithmetic via sinusoidal/Fourier representations is already established by prior work (e.g., Zhou et al., 2024; Kantamneni and Tegmark, 2025; Kadlcík et al., 2025), which slightly tempers the conceptual novelty of the central thesis.

In the activation steering experiments (Section 4.2 and Figure 9), the interpolation coefficient alpha is optimized post-hoc per layer, operation, and probe, which risks overestimating the practical error reduction achievable without a tuned, held-out validation budget.
Several figures (especially Figures 1, 2, 7, 16, and 17) suffer from extremely small font sizes, compressed legends, and low readability when printed or viewed at standard scale.

The layer-dropping intervention described in Section A.8 is evaluated on very few instances and acknowledged to rely on sparse early correct predictions, limiting the generality of layer pruning as a robust correction technique.

strengths: Comprehensive empirical scope: The paper tests across multiple prominent open-weight LLM families (Llama 3/3.1/3.2, OLMo 2, Phi 4) across diverse model scales, systematically validating findings beyond single-model artifacts.

Methodological improvement over prior probing approaches: The proposed parametric sinusoidal probe (param-sin) provides a well-motivated architectural inductive bias by directly learning frequencies, phase shifts, and amplitudes, outperforming existing linear, logarithmic, and previous sinusoidal baselines.

Analysis in natural language contexts: Unlike prior work that predominantly investigates numbers in synthetic, isolated, or templated arithmetic expressions, this work evaluates and trains probes on diverse natural text corpora, demonstrating that natural language training produces significantly better out-of-domain generalization.

Beyond passive observation: The authors connect representational analysis to mechanistic interventions, demonstrating that steering internal activations toward sinusoidal representations can correct arithmetic mistakes across multiplication and division.
weaknesses: Overstated cross-model universality claim: While Section 3.1 shows strong RSA and Fourier frequency overlap in input embeddings, the paper does not test whether probes actually transfer zero-shot across different model families (e.g., evaluating a probe trained on Llama activations directly on OLMo activations). The transfer experiments in Section 3.3 only assess cross-layer transfer within the same model.

Oracle intervention setup: In the activation steering experiments (§4.2 and Figure 9), the patch steering is triggered conditionally when the model is known to fail, and results are reported using the optimal interpolation factor alpha per setup. This demonstrates mechanistic causal relevance but acts as an oracle upper-bound rather than a deployable or practical correction mechanism.

Incremental conceptual framing: The underlying finding that LLMs encode numbers and modular arithmetic via Fourier/sinusoidal features is already established in several cited recent works (e.g., Nanda et al., 2023; Zhou et al., 2024; Kadlcík et al., 2025; Kantamneni and Tegmark, 2025). The contribution here lies mainly in empirical broadening (deeper layers, natural contexts, refined probe design) rather than discovering a fundamentally new representational paradigm.
